title: John Fisher (1535)
hookLine: the only bishop who refused Henry VIII, executed two weeks before More

cards: A thin old man is woken early in a cell in the Tower of London and told that today he will die. The story told by his early biographer is that he asked to sleep a little longer, and slept.
When he rose, he put on his best clothes, and when someone asked why, he said it was his wedding day. He was a bishop, and a cardinal, and he had said no to the King of England.

teach.b: John Fisher was bishop of Rochester and a leader of the university of Cambridge, where he welcomed new learning and brought Erasmus to teach. A scholar and preacher, he was known for living plainly. Then, the question.
King Henry the Eighth wanted his marriage to Catherine of Aragon ended, and then wanted to be named head of the Church in England. Fisher defended the queen's marriage openly.

teach.h: THE OATH HE WOULD NOT TAKE.
teach.b: When the bishops were asked to swear an oath accepting the king's new claims, Catholic memory holds Fisher up as the bishop who would not take it. He was sent to the Tower. Then, the hat.
While he was in prison, Pope Paul the Third named him a cardinal.
Tradition says the king, hearing of it, swore that Fisher would wear the hat on his shoulders, because he would leave him no head to set it on.

teach.h: A WORD FOR THE LAST WALK.
teach.b: Last, the walk. On the way to the scaffold, the story goes, Fisher opened his New Testament and asked for a word to carry with him. It fell open at John's Gospel.

In the Douay-Rheims: "Now this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent." He closed the book and said that was learning enough to last him to his life's end.
Thomas More followed him to the same death shortly after.
Behind both stands a line from Acts, when the apostles were told to stop preaching: "We ought to obey God, rather than men."

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saints John Fisher and Thomas More together in June; in England and Wales, churches, schools and colleges carry their names.

games.q: you're John Fisher, bishop of Rochester. the king's oath is put in front of you, and refusing it means prison. what do you do?
o: sign it, and keep your doubts private.
flee to Rome before anyone notices.
games.why: he refused. he went to the Tower, was made a cardinal there, and was executed shortly before Thomas More.

practice: Think of anyone in charge who is being pushed to bend, a bishop or pastor, a judge, a manager, a teacher, a parent, and choose one.

If you pray, pray for courageous bishops, and for that one person, that they find the steadiness Fisher found. If you don't, simply wish them courage, and notice what it would cost them to stand still.
